text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zambian political parties which attended a two-day inter-party meeting in Stockholm, resolved to resume dialogue to address differences arising from the conduct of controversial elections held last November.
- The central banks urged parliament to pass a law against money laundering to safeguard Zambia against dirty money.
- Hearing of a case in which 27 Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) ex-workers are suing the mining conglomerate for illegal termination of employment starts.
- University of Zambia workers go on strike to push for the dismissal of management, which they accuse of plundering and running down the institution.
